officialReferences.scope: Section 1; preferred source, necessary build/install/run/modify control scripts; exclusions and regenerable material
Source of the actual binaries; exact rebuilt hash not required

criterion.interpretation: Reviewer application of official criteria to retained evidence; not an assertion that every candidate library or tool is included. B does not block by itself; C requires resolution and may expose A requirements.

issues.gap: 35 of the 37 README external-library rows still have no collected source archive in this working set (rubberband and vid.stab collected). Applicable modifications and included transitive sources also need coverage.
issues.closure: Collect the actual preferred source/version and modifications for included components, plus applicable licenses/notices. Hardware/header-only and System Library scope must be resolved rather than assumed.

issues.gap: The publisher identifies custom build scripts but has not supplied the portions controlling generation/installation of the combined binaries. Upstream build systems, selected recipes and saved FFmpeg configure arguments provide partial coverage, not a complete documented build path for this input set.
issues.closure: Include the build/install control scripts and non-regenerable configuration inputs actually needed. Identify selected sources, patches and dependencies; ordinary unmodified available tools need not be archived as corresponding source. Review which original custom portions are necessary; do not demand unrelated machine automation or every historical log.

issues.gap: Actual local modifications/patch selection for core and libraries remain incompletely known. Vanilla CMake is not a blanket no-patch declaration.
issues.closure: Resolve the actual modified source/patch set. A written no-patch statement is one evidence route, not a separately prescribed GPL document. If modifications exist, their preferred source is category A.

issues.gap: Actual included transitive libraries, static/shared selections and System Library/SDK scope remain unresolved; package depends lists do not establish a link graph.
issues.closure: Use selected build inputs, package/source metadata or equivalent evidence to identify actual inclusion and scope. A link map is helpful but not the only acceptable evidence. Collect required sources after classification.

issues.gap: MSYS2 origin is confirmed for bzip2/GnuTLS/libiconv/GMP. Exact recipe commit, architecture and patch selection are not expressly identified; GMP pkgrel 2 remains candidate. fontconfig/XZ MSYS2 provenance is not confirmed.
issues.closure: Tie version-matching recipes/source packages to selected inputs. Keep bzip2 1.0.8-4, GnuTLS 3.8.13-3 and libiconv 1.19-1 version matches distinct from recipe-commit proof; identify GMP package revision.

issues.gap: Repo/commit and vanilla CMake are publisher-confirmed, but selected iconv/ICU/zlib/thread and static/shared configuration is not itemized.
issues.closure: Establish only the selected settings/dependency inputs needed to describe and build the library used. Upstream defaults are evidence about source, not proof of actual choices; necessary configuration becomes A.

issues.gap: Repo/commit and compatibility ON, with all downstream using it, are publisher-confirmed through supplied text. Other selections and modifications are not established.
issues.closure: Use the confirmed compatibility choice in the build description; verify required configuration/patch scope. Apply downstream assertion to Gyan FFmpeg build context only, not yt-dlp or the whole app.

issues.gap: Preferred sources/modifications for confirmed CPython native inputs and required native wheel components are not fully collected. Candidate curl static dependencies remain subject to inclusion/version classification.
issues.closure: Collect the actual sources/patches for required included CPython, native wheel, curl and bootloader components; distinguish separate copies and respect System Library exclusions.

issues.gap: Preferred-source coverage for Meriyah/Astring and the required JS generation inputs is incomplete. EJS TS/config/lock source exists; compiled npm dist alone does not establish preferred source.
issues.closure: Collect missing preferred JS/TS and necessary control/configuration inputs. General-purpose unmodified available build tools are not automatically part of corresponding source.

issues.gap: Release bundle/workflow, custom PyInstaller recipe and CPython build scripts provide partial coverage; necessary control/configuration inputs for unresolved native builds are not yet fully included.
issues.closure: Complete the build/install source path for the actual included native inputs and any non-regenerable generated configuration. No bit-identical rebuild is required.

issues.gap: Selected bootloader/native wheel source and modifications, JS-to-payload correspondence and actual transitive native versions are not fully resolved. No new yt-dlp reply received.
issues.closure: Use existing wheel/DLL hashes, recipes and publisher information to identify source inputs; keep Gyan confirmations separate. A hash comparison can be useful evidence without requiring rebuilt EXE hash identity.

issues.gap: Redistributable terms/notices, System Library scope and platform-union notice entries still require classification.
issues.closure: Determine actual Windows payload and rights/notices. Do not require unrelated OSS source for closed-source runtime DLLs or assume all cross-platform notice entries are included.

issues.gap: Ephemeral config.log, link maps, build logs and package manifests are helpful audit evidence when available; publisher says most ephemeral artifacts were not archived.
issues.closure: Use alternative sufficient source/build descriptions. Missing logs alone do not fail GPL; extract any indispensable non-regenerable configuration/build control into A rather than classifying it as optional.

issues.gap: Exact compiler/runner/environment snapshots improve reproducibility but are not automatically corresponding source.
issues.closure: Record known tool identity if useful. Assess modifications or incorporated runtime components separately under A/C; do not treat every general-purpose tool or compiler source as required.

issues.gap: No rebuild or bit-identical SHA256 comparison has been performed.
issues.closure: GNU FAQ explicitly does not require a rebuild matching the distributed binary hash. Preserve binary identity and source provenance without using this as an acceptance gate.

issues.gap: GMP Mercurial metadata remains inaccessible (historical HTTP 403), but the version-matching MSYS2 recipe uses a checksummed 6.3.0 release tarball, not a Mercurial checkout.
issues.closure: Retire Mercurial full changeset as a standalone blocker for the release-tarball route. Reopen source identity under C only if evidence points to a different checkout; no revision is invented.
